answer: To mint an earning key, an operator must lease a single surveyed transect on a coastal dune field and seat a uniquely serialled ferrous probe whose length and alloy batch are sealed at the mill. Only the leaseholder may energize a surface hammer at a surprise tick; a buried geophone captures the returning echo. The registrar matches mill stamp, lease plot, and the echo's travel-time curve. Cloning identities therefore requires buying another exclusive transect and commissioning another one-shot ferrous pour for each fake agent, plus being on the sand when the hammer falls.
